newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan business sees little impact from Deng death.
newsitem.headline: Japan business sees little impact from Deng death.

text.p: Japanese business leaders said on Thursday that they foresaw little change in Sino-Japan ties following the death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.
Kosaku Inaba, chairman of the Japan Chamber of Commerce and Industry, said Deng was a giant who played a major role in Chinese history, Kyodo news agency reported.
But Inaba added that no confusion in two-way ties was likely, because the reforms he introduced were well under way.
Shoichiro Toyoda, chairman of business lobby Keidanren, echoed that view.

"China's development was carried out largely through his (Deng's) reform and liberalisation of the country," Kyodo quoted Toyoda as saying. "Even after his death, the basic policy of the nation will continue to prevail and the economy will continue to grow," Toyoda added.

Sino-Japanese economic ties are also expected to be unaffected by Deng's demise because Beijing is shifting to collective leadership under President Jiang Zemin and will continue to follow its socialist market economic policies, Kyodo quoted the business leaders as saying.
Tokyo share prices, meanwhile, were expected to be little moved by the news of Deng's death.

Brokers said Tokyo stock investors were paying more attention to matters such as the direction of shares in multinational blue-chip firms, which have been supporting the market recently but which on Wednesday fell prey to some profit-taking.
"The Tokyo stock market will probably pay little attention," said Paul Migliorato, a senior salesman at Jardine Fleming Securities.

"I think they are more concerned with the fate of Sony than with that of Deng Xiaoping. What matters most to investors is that blue chips have supported the market so far, and that will be the market focus," Migliorato said.
Foreign exchange traders in Tokyo said the dollar was also unlikely to react to Deng's death here, because the news was announced when the New York market was still open.
Deng died late on Wednesday of complications from Parkinson's disease and a lung infection. The announcement of his death was made by the Communist Party.
